## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

No correctness issue was found at `f1631da5`. The notes below are small visual, documentation and test points.

**Verified** (source review plus isolated parser and lint runs; rendering was not executed):

| Area | Result |
|---|---|
| Solid themes | Unchanged. `fillSpec` is null for every `BorderSurface` except `PopupCard` and `KeyboardPanel`, and a single-token value keeps the native `Rectangle` fill and border. |
| Layering | Fill, then border, then content. Any non-empty border moves to the overlay in gradient mode, so it is not painted beneath the fill. |
| Rounded edges | The `FillOverlay` outline matched the border ring's outer contour in 175 synthetic width/height/radius combinations. |
| Parsing | 2 to 10 stops, optional angle (`0deg` left to right, `90deg` top to bottom), whole-value and per-stop references with cycle and missing-key fallback, `background-alpha` multiplied once per stop. |
| `flatColor` | Head falls back cleanly where `quattro` throws a binding error on malformed hex such as `#broken`, or overflows the stack on a two-key reference cycle. |
| Tests | `popup-gradient-test.sh` passes 24/24 on head and fails on the merge-base. `FillOverlay.qml` passes `qmllint` against Qt 6.11.2 with no warnings. |

### Slider cut-out marks become visible on gradient cards

`PanelSlider` draws its tick marks and knob ring in `bar.background`, relying on that color matching the card (`shell/Ui/PanelSlider.qml:21-26`, knob border at line 89). The default template gives `[bar]` and `[popups]` the same opaque background, so these blend in today. On a gradient card they no longer match:

```text
default solid card:   card = popups.background = bar.background  -> tick ends and knob ring blend in
gradient card:        card = gradient stops ≠ bar.background     -> ~2px tick ends and knob ring show
```

Affected: the audio panel sliders (knob ring) and the monitor text-size slider (seven ticks plus knob ring). The same contrast already appears on `quattro` when a theme sets `[popups] background` different from `[bar] background`, so this exposes an existing assumption rather than breaking solid themes. The effect depends on stop colors and position, and was identified from source only, not observed on screen.

**Impact:** small bar-colored marks and rings on audio and monitor panels when a gradient is set.

**Suggested change:** derive the slider cut-out color from the host card, or make the ticks and knob ring transparent outside the track. Alternatively, check the audio and monitor panels visually and accept the marks as intended.

**Documentation:** Three wording points:

- `docs/theming.md` says "Menus ... are not gradient consumers", but the tray right-click menu (`Tray.qml:521`) is a `PopupCard` and receives the gradient. Naming the main `[menu]` surface would avoid the ambiguity, and the same applies to the PR description.
- Color-only consumers of `Color.popups.background` take the first stop's color with `background-alpha` *replacing* its alpha (the solid rule). The rendered first stop *multiplies* them. With a first stop such as `#11223380`, consumers get alpha 1.0 while the card edge renders at about 0.5; with `transparent`, consumers get opaque black. In first-party code this only affects the 1px Tailscale warning badge ring. A sentence stating which alpha rule color-only consumers follow would make the docs match.
- The `flatColor` change applies to every `Color` role, not only popups. Qt-only `#RRRGGGBBB` and `#RRRRGGGGBBBB` values that rendered on `quattro` now fall back to the role default. One line in the PR description would cover it.

**Optional test improvement:** A diagnostic copy with the new `flatColor` cycle guard removed still passes all 24 assertions. The existing cycle case is a whole-value reference, which `fillSpec`'s own loop resolves first. An assertion on a per-stop cycle (`background = "fill.a #445566"` with `fill.a` and `fill.b` referencing each other), or on `composed()` with a cyclic value, would cover the guard. Separately, the assertion that `Color.qml` does not contain `fillSpec("menu.background"` will fail once #7748 is reconciled, because that PR adds exactly that call. A positive check of this PR's popup wiring would avoid making the two features mutually exclusive in tests.
